newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi Arabia recognises Taleban Afghan government.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia recognises Taleban Afghan government.

text.p: Saudi Arabia on Monday became the second country after Pakistan to recognise the Taleban Islamic movement's government in Afghanistan, the Saudi Press Agency (SPA) said.

"The government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia decided to recognise the Taleban government following the latest developments in Afghanistan," said an official statement carried by SPA after a regular weekly cabinet meeting.

It was referring to weekend military gains by Taleban's Islamic militia which tightened its grip on northern Afghanistan as routed opposition warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum fled to Turkey. The movement captured the capital Kabul last September.
Pakistan gave the Taleban vital support on Sunday by recognising the movement's government.

"The Saudi council of ministers wishes the Taleban government all success in restoring peace, security and stability to brotherly Afghanistan and looks forward to continuing good bilateral relations," SPA quoted the statement as saying.
Saudi Arabia, home to Islam's two holiest shrines, gave generous financial support to the Moslem Afghan Mujahideen who defeated Soviet troops in the late 1980s.
Some diplomats said Saudi Arabia's Gulf Arab neighbours were expected to follow Riyadh's move by extending recognition to the Taleban government.
